note: Preface 1990-91: Kolhua, Harsh-ka-Tila (Thanesar) and Lalitagiri listed among the year's excavations; detail in 805-806.

author: L. C. Singh, Excavation Branch III, Patna, ASI
name_in_asr: Kolhua: Main Stupa, Asokan pillar, brick-lined tank
asr_identification: Kolhua (Muzaffarpur): main stupa beside the Asokan pillar; brick-lined tank 20 m S of the pillar
evidence: 1990-91: ayakas of the last phase of the main stupa; closely set votive stupas round the pillar over a Gupta lime floor; a brick-lined tank 20 m S of the pillar partly exposed, a drain from the votive stupas running into it; in Area B a massive shrine with a chaitya behind, later turned into living rooms, inside an enclosure wall; finds from NBP to Gupta levels, an amulet in Asokan Brahmi, a 'ye dhamma' sealing, a terracotta of the Buddha's birth
quote: A brick-lined tank (pl. III A), … 20 m south of the Asokan pillar, was partly exposed. A burnt brick drain, coming from the side of the votive stupas, was found terminating in this tank
note: First exposure of the tank S of the pillar and stupa, which matches Xuanzang's monkey tank (Mizutani 07.03.04; study: Kolhua pillar and stupa, secure); the report does not name Xuanzang or the tank's legend. Continued in 673 (1991-92), 523 (1992-93) and 816 (1993-94).

author: B. M. Pande, Institute of Archaeology, ASI
evidence: 1990-91: Kushana mud rampart (two phases, c. 15 m wide) traced on the S slope; small PGW settlement only; Post-Gupta or Vardhana deposits reveal an earlier phase of the large building-complex (terracotta seal, moulds, couchant lion); Rajput-level palatial complexes of 9 and 7 rooms round a brick-paved court, destroyed by fire
quote: This season's excavation of the Post-Gupta or Vardhana deposits, though confined to a small area, revealed an earlier phase of construction of the large building-complex partly exposed in previous seasons.
note: Continues 472 and 493: Vardhana (Harsha's dynasty) building activity of Xuanzang's time on the mound; Thanesar = Sthanesvara is assumed, as Mizutani 04.08 and the study (secure). No Buddhist remains; Xuanzang's stupa NW of the city not touched.
Epigraphy: Eastern Chalukya copper plates in the Amaravati museum (from Duddukuru and Chamarru); no identification.

Treasure trove and discoveries: Ikshvaku lead coins, a 2nd-c. label inscription and crystal relic caskets from debris clearance at the Amaravati Mahastupa; nothing on the Dhanyakataka capital or Purvasaila (10.14, 10.14.02a). Piprahwa not in the passage's text.
Chance find of gold and ritual objects W of the main shrine at Sarnath; radiocarbon list. No identification.
Museums (Amaravati, Bodhgaya, Bombay, Calcutta).
Conservation (Sirpur Lakshmana temple museum courtyard; Lalitagiri and Udayagiri, Cuttack, fencing and repairs).
Conservation (Amaravati stupa drum wall; Kalingapatnam brick stupa; Guntupalle).
Conservation (Sahet-Mahet stupa, Pakki-Kuti, Kachchi-Kuti).
Chemical conservation (Sarnath Monastery 1, Bodhgaya museum, Mathura).
Archaeological gardens (Nagarjunakonda etc.).

author: Excavation Branch III, Patna, ASI
asr_identification: seven-tier brick-lined tank at Kolhua, c. 65 x 33 m, S of the Asokan pillar
evidence: 1993-94: the tank exposed completely: c. 65 x 33 m, seven tiers, bathing ghats on the W and S arms, a retaining wall c. 1 m wide all round; the NW part built differently, with offsets every two courses; no dating given
quote: carried out excavation at Kolhua (near Vaishali) with a view to exposing the ancient tank completely. … The tank measures approximately 65 X 33 m, having two bathing ghats along the western
note: Completes 805, 673 and 523: the tank S of the pillar = Xuanzang's monkey tank (Mizutani 07.03.04; study secure), not said by the report; no date for the tank in this season.
Kunal excavation (pre-Harappan); Thanesar named only on the course of the Sarasvati.

author: M. Acharya, Department of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Haryana
asr_identification: Sugh, c. 5 km E of Jagadhri, in village Amadalpur (Yamuna Nagar)
evidence: Eight quadrants; cultural deposit 2.10 m; Period I (5th-1st c. BC) grey, black-slipped and black-polished wares with two NBPW sherds, ring-wells; Period II (1st c. BC-3rd c. AD) red ware, stamped pottery, Sunga-Kushan terracottas, mud-brick and baked-brick walls, a plaque of a child learning the alphabet; nothing later reported
quote: Sugh (30°9' N; 77° 23'E), situated about 5 km east of Jagadhri … enjoyed considerable importance during ancient times when it was known as Srughna. … The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang found an Asokan pillar and a monastery here in the seventh century.
note: Names Xuanzang. Sugh = Srughna as Cunningham (asr), Mizutani 04.09 and the study (secure, 5 km E of Jagadhri; the table's Mizutani gloss 'near Kalsi, Dehra Dun' does not fit, as noted at 160). The excavated sequence stops at the 3rd c. AD, so it shows nothing of Xuanzang's time or of his pillar and monastery. Cf. 160, 191 (the 'Sugha' sealing).

author: L. C. Singh, Excavation Branch III, Patna, ASI, with the Archaeological Research Institute, Kansai University
asr_identification: Mahet (Bahraich), N part of the Surajkund area
evidence: 1993-94: two structural phases; three house complexes inside an enclosure wall, community wells and ring-wells; terracottas incl. small Buddha heads and mithuna plaques; iron and copper objects, coins; Period I late NBP ended by a flood, Period II Gupta, Period III late Gupta with a shrunken settlement
quote: resumed excavation at Mahet (Sravasti) in the vicinity of Surajkund area … Period III- late Gupta period with a Shrunk settlement
note: Mahet = Sravasti as Mizutani 06.01 and the study (secure). The shrunken late Gupta settlement fits the ruined city Xuanzang describes, but the report does not say so; no inscription.
Discoveries: Ikshvaku lead coins at the Amaravati Mahachaitya; a 12th-c. door-frame from Vadnagar; no identification.
Sanghol custard-apple remains; museums (Allahabad).
Museums (Mathura, Nagarjunakonda, Ratnagiri, Sarnath).
Conservation (Harsh-ka-Tila and Sheikh Chilli's tomb, Thanesar).
Conservation (Kolhua tank, Nalanda Temple 13, Kushinagar Mathakuar shrine, Sarnath Chaukhandi and Dhamekh).
Archaeological chemistry (bat excreta in the Ajanta caves).
Plate list 1953-54 (Salihundam, Kanchipuram, Sirpur); excavations coded elsewhere.
Plate list 1954-55 (Tamluk, Nagarjunakonda, Sirpur); excavations coded elsewhere.
Nagar mounds at Somnath: Period V with Gupta and Valabhi coins; Nevasa. Not the Valabhi site (11.08).
Nagda excavation, District Ujjain (chalcolithic); not Ujjain city.
Title page (frontispiece Ujjain) and general introduction 1956-57.

author: N. R. Banerjee, Excavations Branch, Department of Archaeology
asr_identification: Garh-Kalika mound on the N outskirts of Ujjain
evidence: 1956-57: occupation from before 600 BC to the 14th c. in four Periods (35-40 ft of deposit); a Period I mud rampart with moat (moat c. 80 ft wide, 22 ft deep) enclosing c. 1 x 3/4 mile, the Sipra on the W and N; a PGW sherd in the rampart core; breached by floods three times in Period II and revetted in brick
quote: the Garh-Kalika mound, representing the ancient Ujjayini, on the northern outskirts of the city of Ujjain in Madhya Pradesh … The excavation revealed a continuity of occupation on the site from a date prior to 600 B.C. to the beginning of Muslim rule in Malwa in the fourteenth century
note: Ujjain = Ujjayini (11.12) as Mizutani and the study (probable): the old city was occupied through Xuanzang's time. Nothing on his monasteries (mostly ruined) or the Asoka 'hell' stupa near the city. Continued in 835-836.
Explorations: microlithic sites near Ujjain, Karad, Karla; no identification.
Plate list 1956-57 (Ujjain, Kausambi, Chandraketugarh, Jaugada); excavations coded in 831.
Motidharai, 10 miles NE of Valabhipur: Harappan and early historical; Khandivli survey. Not Valabhi itself.

author: N. R. Banerjee, Excavations Branch, Department of Archaeology
asr_identification: Garh-Kalika mound on the outskirts of Ujjain
evidence: 1957-58: the mud fortifications belong to a citadel (rampart 245 ft at the base, moat 152 ft wide), ordinary houses outside; Period I c. 700-500 BC (iron, black-slipped wares), timber-reinforced riverside wall; Period II c. 500-200 BC brick lining of the moat; moat narrowed in Period III
quote: Kalika mound on the outskirts of Ujjain … This year's work revealed that the mud-fortifications, first exposed last year, belonged to a citadel, the humbler habitations being in the undefended areas outside.
note: Early periods of the Ujjayini citadel (11.12; Mizutani, study: Ujjain); nothing of the 7th c. in this part of the report. See 836.

author: N. R. Banerjee, Excavations Branch, Department of Archaeology
name_in_asr: Ujjain (Ozene of the Periplus); casket-lid of Nagabudhi the pravrajita
evidence: 1957-58: Period III bead- and iron-working; Period II apsidal stone structure, brick tank, 45-ft well; an ivory seal 'gothajasa tisakasa' (3rd-2nd c. BC); in Period III a terracotta casket-lid inscribed 'Nagabudhisa pravajitasa' (1st c. AD), i.e. of a Buddhist monk; Period IV a 10-ft deposit with Muslim coins, much disturbed
quote: a casket-lid and a seal, both of terracotta, bearing respectively the inscriptions Nagabudhisa pravajitasa and Asadevasa in Brahmi characters of the first century A.D.
note: A monk's casket-lid shows Buddhists at Ujjayini by the 1st c. AD; Xuanzang (11.12) found dozens of monasteries there, mostly ruined, and a few hundred monks. The post-Gupta levels (Period IV) are disturbed and yield nothing of his time. Agrees with Mizutani and the study (Ujjain).
Plate list 1957-58 (Ujjain, Ratnagiri).

author: D. Mitra, Eastern Circle, Department of Archaeology
asr_identification: Ratnagiri hill, Cuttack district (now Jajpur), N of the main stupa
evidence: 1958-59: two full monasteries side by side facing S; Monastery 1 c. 180 ft square with a pancha-ratha front, porch flanked by images of Vajrapani and Lokesvara, a chlorite door-frame with Gaja-Lakshmi, images of Jambhala, Hariti, Ganga and Yamuna
quote: Excavation revealed two full-fledged monasteries which, notwithstanding their normal monastic plans, had several remarkable features.
note: A large monastic site N of the Mahanadi, inside the study's Odra (10.09: N Orissa, capital most often Jajpur; Mizutani: capital undecided). No date in this part; the name evidence is in 839.

author: D. Mitra, Eastern Circle, Department of Archaeology
evidence: Monastery 2 later than the first period of Monastery 1; bronze-casting centre (images of Buddha, Tara, Jambhala); hundreds of clay sealings, some naming the monastery Ratnagiri; the Main Stupa built over an earlier brick structure; a second stupa base with dharani plaques; Taranatha's Ratnagiri recalled
quote: A number of terracotta sealings with the legend sri-Ratnagiri-mahavihariy-arya-bhikshu-samghasya (pl. XLVIII A), found in the excavation, indicated that this Buddhist establishment had been known as Ratnagiri, a name which persists even now.
note: Inscribed sealings name the monastery Ratnagiri, not Puspagiri: this tells against Ratnagiri as Xuanzang's Puspagiri (10.09.02; Mizutani Khandagiri, study Udayagiri-Khandagiri; Lalitagiri proposed at 702). It confirms a great monastery in Odra N of the Mahanadi (10.09). The sealings are not dated here and Xuanzang is not named.

author: D. Mitra, Eastern Circle, Department of Archaeology
asr_identification: apsidal laterite structure on the top of Udayagiri hill, Bhubaneswar
evidence: 1958-59: apsidal structure 78 ft 1 in long, 46 ft wide, of large laterite blocks, with a circular wall inside its apse, laterite and rock floor, post-holes for a tiled roof on posts, a rock-cut drain; the circle later turned into an apsidal shrine
quote: an excavation of the area was undertaken to expose them by the Eastern Circle of the Department, under Shrimati D. Mitra. The ruins consisted of an apsidal structure (fig. 17; pl. L A) with an axial length of 78 ft. 1 in., and basal width of 46 ft.
note: The building on the hill Mizutani and the study take for Puspagiri (10.09.02) or the NW hill monastery (10.09.02a); its affiliation is argued in 841.

author: D. Mitra, Eastern Circle, Department of Archaeology
asr_identification: Jaina apsidal shrine on Udayagiri; Udayagiri and Khandagiri held to contain only Jaina monuments
evidence: Later square platform over the circle; red ill-baked pottery and a neolithic celt only; the excavator calls the shrine Jaina, the first apsidal structure in Orissa, perhaps built by Kharavela (1st c. BC), since the two hills hold monuments of no other faith
quote: There can be no doubt that it was a religious edifice of Jaina affiliation, as the Udayagiri and the adjacent Khandagiri hills contain monuments of no other faith.
note: Differs from the study: the dig finds only a Jaina shrine, and the excavator states that Udayagiri-Khandagiri have no Buddhist monuments, against Mizutani's Khandagiri and the study's Udayagiri-Khandagiri for the Buddhist Puspagiri monastery (10.09.02) and Udayagiri for the NW hill monastery (10.09.02a). The Buddhist Udayagiri in Cuttack (Jajpur) district, beside Lalitagiri and Ratnagiri, is a different site. Weakens 10.09.02 and 10.09.02a.
Conservation (Salihundam, Sankaram, Sirpur Lakshmana temple).
Conservation (Ajanta, Pitalkhora, Karla; Sindhudurg in Ratnagiri district, Maharashtra).
Plate list 1958-59 (Ratnagiri, Udayagiri, Kausambi, Sravasti).

author: K. V. Soundara Rajan, assisted by S. C. Ray, Western Circle, Department of Archaeology
asr_identification: town-mound at Broach on the Narmada
evidence: 1959-60: Period I (from c. 3rd c. BC) black-and-red ware, one NBPW sherd, mud rampart with ditch, ring-wells, a large bead industry; Period II Red Polished Ware, Kshatrapa lead and copper coins, a 6th-7th c. chaturmukha-linga, rampart revetted in brick, lasting without a break to the 7th-8th c.; Period III medieval after a break
quote: excavated at the town-mound at Broach, the ancient Bharukachchha of Indian literature and Barygaza of the classical geographers … This Period, represented by a 10-ft. thick deposit, appears to have extended without break almost to the seventh-eighth century A.D.
note: Broach = Bharukaccha (11.04) as Mizutani and the study (probable): a walled town occupied without break through Xuanzang's time. No Buddhist find. The passage goes on to the Devnimori stupa (Sabarkantha), not tied to a Xiyu ji place here.

author: D. Mitra, Eastern Circle, Department of Archaeology
evidence: 1959-60: deep foundations of Monastery 1 on the hill slope; Monastery 2 built over an earlier monastery (bronzes in its secret chamber), itself over a still earlier wing of four cells; two brick rekha temples SE of Monastery 1
quote: Monastery 2 was found to have been built over the ruined walls of an earlier monastery, utilized as the foundation at most places
note: Two monastic phases below Monastery 2, undated in the report, show the site's depth of occupation; bears on Odra (10.09) only as a great monastery N of the Mahanadi (see 839).
Explorations in Madhya Pradesh (Eran, Rajota near Ujjain, Vidisha) and Maharashtra; no identification.
Conservation (Ghantasala, Udayagiri hill-fort in Nellore, Alampur).
